title: Game Design
description:
One artifact covering scope, session, retention, monetization, progression and economy.

These are NOT separate stages and not separate documents. Scope depends on monetization, which depends on session, which depends on scope — sequencing them invents an order that does not exist, and splitting them into four files guarantees they drift apart. One artifact with a recorded consistency result is atomic; four files cannot be.

The `consistency` block is what makes 'these were co-designed' checkable rather than asserted. It is produced by evaluating core/reference/design-consistency-rules.yaml and is the exit guard on title:design.

The human-readable GDD is a RENDERING of this artifact (see core/templates/gdd.md), not a separate source of truth.

core_loop.description: The repeating unit of play, stated as a cycle. If it cannot be written as a loop, it is not one.

pillars.description: Two or three. More than three means none of them decide anything.

tiers.description: Explicit scope tiers. The factory must be able to say 'this feature is excluded because it does not contribute enough to initial validation' — and that sentence needs somewhere to live.

content_units.description: Countable content: levels, maps, enemy types, puzzle sets. The number the consistency rules check against session length.

progression_terminal.description: How progression ends, or an explicit statement that it loops. Open-ended progression is an endless content obligation.

session.description: Explicit because it is the thing most often left implicit and then contradicted by the monetization plan. Values depend on genre, audience, platform and monetization — there are no universal numbers, which is why none are defaulted here.

time_to_first_play_s.description: From load to the player doing something. Web portal traffic has no install cost anchoring it, so this is unforgiving.

structure.description: How a session begins, escalates and ends. A session that ends arbitrarily reads as being interrupted.

reward_moments_per_session.description: Natural points where the player wants something. Rewarded video only works at these, which is why the consistency rules check it.

return_reason.description: Why a player opens this again tomorrow, in their words rather than in mechanics.

monetization.description: Designed before production, not retrofitted. Platform-aware: game code calls the template's platform abstraction, never a portal SDK directly.

trigger.description: The in-game moment. 'On death, offer a continue' — not 'every 90 seconds'.

player_value.description: What the player gets. Required thinking for rewarded placements: if the answer is nothing, it is an interstitial wearing a costume.

asset_requirements.description: The assets the design needs, by kind. The asset manifest is built from this list; when it is absent a baseline is derived from screens, audio direction and locales, which is a floor, not a design. Kinds are the keys of core/reference/asset-policy.yaml.

source.description: The intended final source. Absent means library first, then procedural.

tags.description: Words a library search matches on.

frames.description: For a spritesheet or an animation.

existing.description: An asset already chosen, with where it came from. Its license and origin are checked like any other external asset's.

path.description: Relative to the game repository root.

platform_constraints_applied.description: Which binding platform requirements this design absorbed, and how. Populated from the pinned platform profiles. An empty list on a title with required platforms means the profiles were not read.

consistency.description: The recorded result of evaluating core/reference/design-consistency-rules.yaml. Exit guard on title:design.

warnings_acknowledged.description: Set at G3. A warning nobody read is just a comment.

open_questions.description: Things the prototype is expected to answer. Better recorded than silently assumed.
